title: Ice Cream Parlour
strapline: One scoop or two? Sprinkles on top?
intent: A parlour is a warm, familiar shop children know from real life, so the play starts confidently and quickly gets rich.
Serving customers is a natural conversation with a real purpose — taking an order, checking the flavour, saying how much.
Money, counting and 'how many scoops' bring early number into play without a worksheet in sight.
Choosing, scooping and decorating stretches fine motor control and lots of decision-making.
There is real writing to do — order pads, a flavour menu, price signs, a 'closed/open' sign.
implementation: Set up a proper counter with tubs of 'ice cream' (pom-poms, playdough, coloured balls), cones, scoops and a till.
Take the customer role so children serve, count scoops and handle the money.
Model the shop talk: 'Could I have two scoops of strawberry in a cone, please?' 'That'll be three pounds.'
Add real number reasons — prices, how many scoops, one for each person in the family.
Leave order pads, a menu and coins so writing and counting have a job to do.
Extend the story: a queue at the parlour, a birthday order, running out of a flavour, a delivery arriving.
key_questions: What flavours have you got today — which is your favourite?
How many scoops would this customer like, and how much will that be?
What could you write on the order so you don't forget it?
The strawberry has run out — what will you tell your customer?
How will people know when your parlour is open?

impact.text: Children serve customers in role, taking orders and holding a genuine back-and-forth conversation.
Children count scoops, coins and customers, and use 'more', 'another' and early number words for real.
Children handle money and prices in play, matching coins to a cost and giving change.
Children scoop, decorate and hand over the cones with careful, controlled hands.
Children 'write' orders, menus and price signs and read them back to the customer.
Children take turns as server and customer, wait in the queue and sort out who is next.

enhancements: Playdough and a real scoop for making and serving cones.
A till, coins and a card machine for paying.
Order pads, a flavour menu, price labels and an open/closed sign.
Empty (clean) tubs and cones from home to make it real.
Pom-poms, coloured balls or beads as scoops in different flavours.
A birthday-order challenge: a family wants six different scoops — can you get it right?

playing_exploring: Children draw on a well-known real experience and step confidently into running the shop.
They test the props — how the scoop works, how the till opens — as they play.
active_learning: Children keep the parlour going through a busy queue, serving customer after customer.
creating_thinking: Children solve real problems in role — a sold-out flavour, a big order, working out the total.
